newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot domestic natgas eases, exports rise.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot domestic natgas eases, exports rise.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices on Tuesday softened further in Alberta but recovered in the export markets on the heels of a NYMEX rally, traders said.

Spot gas at the AECO storage in Alberta was talked about one cent lower at C$1.39-1.41 per gigajoule. September AECO slipped to about C$1.40, while September/October business hovered around C$1.45-1.46, traders said.

"There's an outage on Great Lakes (Transmission) today and tomorrow. That's backing some gas into Alberta," one Calgary-based trader said, referring to the system that connects with TransCanada Pipelines at the Emerson export point and near Niagara.
At Sumas, Wash., prices were up about seven cents at $1.05-1.06 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) due to rising temperatures in the Northwest and heftier electricity prices.
At Niagara, prices were also several cents higher in the mid-$2.40s per mmBtu as NYMEX's September gas futures rose to a high of $2.42, gaining another 4.6 cents from Monday.
